realLife: Before choosing a model, plot your data. If the groups wrap around each other, a linear model is the wrong tool.
summary: Different models carve the plane in different ways. Compare them on the same points.
headline: Every model draws its own map
overview: A classifier is a rule that colours every spot on the plane. The shape of its boundary shows what it can and cannot express.
A straight line cannot separate groups arranged like the corners of XOR. A curved model, a tree or nearest neighbours can.

break.label: Break it
break.explains: Pick XOR with a straight-line model. No line can separate it, so accuracy stays near a coin flip.

check.question: Why does a straight-line model fail on XOR?
options: No single line separates the groups

data: Four shapes: two blobs, two moons, a ring inside a ring, and XOR corners. Same 160 points per shape, 70/30 split. Curved means logistic regression on x, y and their squares and product.
maths: A linear model's boundary is the set where w·x + b = 0, a straight line in two dimensions.
Adding squares and products of the inputs lets the same model draw ellipses and hyperbolas.
kNN and trees draw boundaries without a formula: patchwork regions built from the data.

from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures
m = make_pipeline(PolynomialFeatures(2), LogisticRegression())
